henry.title: Haiku: A Poem in 17 Claps
henry.intro: Japan gave the world a tiny poem called a haiku. You'll write one about autumn. (About 15 minutes.)
steps: 📖 Read Basho's frog haiku. Count the lines.
🍂 Pick autumn words from the word bank.
links: Read the first sentence, then find Basho's frog poem.

passage.text: 📜 A haiku is a short poem from Japan. It has 3 lines.
passage.q: How many lines does a haiku have?

passage.text: 👏 Each clap in a word is a syllable. A haiku has 5, then 7, then 5 syllables.
passage.q: How many claps in the middle line?

passage.text: 🐸 Basho lived in Japan over 300 years ago. His famous haiku is about a frog jumping into an old pond.
🍂 Many haiku have a season word, like leaves for autumn. Here's one: Red leaves drifting down / crunching under my two feet / autumn says hello

worksheet: Clap it, circle the claps: leaf 1 / 2 / 3  ·  pumpkin 1 / 2 / 3  ·  October 1 / 2 / 3
Basho's haiku is about a ____. Circle: frog / fish
henry.challenge: Write a second haiku about Halloween (it's tomorrow!). Read it out loud in one breath.

frankie.title: Lucky Cat Words 🐱☀️
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud: In Japan, a lucky cat statue waves hello. Japan's flag is a red sun! Let's read and write cat, sun and cup. (About 14 minutes.)
steps: 👀 Say the picture words together: cat, sun, cup.
🔤 Sound out c-a-t. Tap one finger for each sound.
🃏 Match word cards to things at home.
✏️ Trace, then write: I can see a cat. (stretch!)

handsOn.title: 🃏 Word-card hunt
steps: ✍️ Grown-up writes cat, sun, cup on 3 cards, big letters.
👆 Frankie taps each letter and says the sound: c… a… t… cat!
🏠 Put each card next to a match: a cup, a toy cat or picture, a sunny window.
🔁 Mix the cards. Can he read them without help?
handsOn.look: Grown-up: say each sound slowly, then blend fast. Point under each letter as he reads.
handsOn.q: Match the words to pictures on the sheet.
